findings.title: Sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not sort
findings.scenario: The board [{player:'a',points:1},{player:'b',points:5},{player:'c',points:3},{player:'d',points:9}] with count 3 should give d, b, c. The comparator only ever returns true or false, which become 1 or 0, never a negative number. V8's insertion sort reads 0 and 1 as 'keep the current order', so the board comes back in insertion order and the result is a, b, c. The leaderboard shows the wrong players.
findings.whyNotPrevented: Array.prototype.sort accepts any comparator, there is no type checking, and no test calls topPlayers (Grep 'topPlayers' finds only the definition).

findings.title: Sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not sort by points
findings.scenario: board = [{player:'a',points:1},{player:'b',points:2}]. The comparator returns false (0) or true (1) and never a negative number. V8's sort calls cmp(b, a), gets 2<1 = false = 0, and leaves the order as it is. topPlayers returns [a(1), b(2)], so the lowest scorer comes first. With more entries the order is effectively arbitrary, and higher scorers can fall outside the top `count`.
findings.whyNotPrevented: Array.prototype.sort coerces the boolean to 0 or 1 without any error. The project has no type checking and no tests for topPlayers (Grep 'topPlayers' found only src/leaderboard.js).

findings.title: TTL in seconds is added to a timestamp in milliseconds, so sessions expire about 1000x too early
